units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
You should go to bed, Miss Mabel.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Lord Goring!
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: My father told me to go to bed an hour ago. I don’t see why I shouldn’t give you the same advice. I always pass on good advice. It is the only thing to do with it. It is never of any use to oneself.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Lord Goring, you are always ordering me out of the room. I think it most courageous of you. Especially as I am not going to bed for hours.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Goes over to the sofa .
You can come and sit down if you like, and talk about anything in the world, except the Royal Academy, Mrs. Cheveley, or novels in Scotch dialect. They are not improving subjects.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Catches sight of something that is lying on the sofa half hidden by the cushion .
What is this? Some one has dropped a diamond brooch! Quite beautiful, isn’t it?
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Shows it to him .

I wish it was mine, but Gertrude won’t let me wear anything but pearls, and I am thoroughly sick of pearls. They make one look so plain, so good and so intellectual. I wonder whom the brooch belongs to.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: I wonder who dropped it.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: It is a beautiful brooch.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: It is a handsome bracelet.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: It isn’t a bracelet. It’s a brooch.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: It can be used as a bracelet.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Takes it from her , and , pulling out a green letter-case , puts the ornament carefully in it , and replaces the whole thing in his breast-pocket with the most perfect sang froid .
What are you doing?
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Miss Mabel, I am going to make a rather strange request to you.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Eagerly .
Oh, pray do! I have been waiting for it all the evening.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Is a little taken aback , but recovers himself .
Don’t mention to anybody that I have taken charge of this brooch. Should any one write and claim it, let me know at once.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: That is a strange request.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Well, you see I gave this brooch to somebody once, years ago.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: You did?
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Yes.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: LADY CHILTERN enters alone .
The other guests have gone .
Then I shall certainly bid you good-night. Good-night, Gertrude!
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Exit .
Good-night, dear!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: To LORD GORING.
You saw whom Lady Markby brought here to-night?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Yes. It was an unpleasant surprise. What did she come here for?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Apparently to try and lure Robert to uphold some fraudulent scheme in which she is interested. The Argentine Canal, in fact.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: She has mistaken her man, hasn’t she?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: She is incapable of understanding an upright nature like my husband’s!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Yes. I should fancy she came to grief if she tried to get Robert into her toils. It is extraordinary what astounding mistakes clever women make.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I don’t call women of that kind clever. I call them stupid!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Same thing often. Good-night, Lady Chiltern!
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Good-night!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Enter SIR ROBERT CHILTERN.
My dear Arthur, you are not going? Do stop a little!
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Afraid I can’t, thanks. I have promised to look in at the Hartlocks’. I believe they have got a mauve Hungarian band that plays mauve Hungarian music. See you soon. Good-bye!
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Exit
How beautiful you look to-night, Gertrude!
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN
